newsitem.title: CHINA: Beijing vows no change on HK entry for Chinese.
newsitem.headline: Beijing vows no change on HK entry for Chinese.

text.p: Beijing will maintain tight restrictions on Chinese visiting or migrating to Hong Kong even after British colonial rule in the territory ends on June 30, the China Daily said on Tuesday.

Rules governing travel between the mainland and Hong Kong would not change after sovereignty returned to China, the official newspaper quoted Zhu Jianmin, chief of the Hong Kong division of the Exit Entry Administration Bureau, as saying.
Chinese who believed that travelling to Hong Kong after the midnight handover would be as easy as visiting Shenzhen in nearby Guangdong province were wrong, Zhu said.
Many Hong Kong residents say they fear the return to Chinese rule could unleash a torrent of economic migration as workers from the mainland rush to join the territory's booming economy.
Only 150 people a day would be granted one-way permits allowing them to live in Hong Kong from July 1, the same as the current quota, China Daily quoted Zhu as saying.
The border between Guangdong province and Hong Kong would become an administrative line, with customs inspections remaining in force, he said.
Illegal immigrants caught in Hong Kong would continue to be returned to the mainland, he said.

A senior Chinese official was quoted as saying earlier this month that Beijing would have the final say on migration from the mainland to Hong Kong after the end of more than 150 years of British colonial rule.

It would be difficult for the future government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to know who was qualified for entry, the South China Morning Post quoted deputy director of the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office Chen Ziqing as saying.
Beijing wanted to ensure that the desire of many Chinese to visit Hong Kong did not disturb life in the territory, but entry would be a mere formality for working officials, Chen said.
